subject: Coefficient of determination as a goodness of fit for CFAs

messages.author: b7f09e3ed25070f4
messages.subject: Coefficient of determination as a goodness of fit for CFAs
parts:
Hi all,

For those who has extensive experience of conducting CFAs, have you ever come across the coefficient of determination (CD) being used as a goodness of fit measure for CFAs? 

Recently, I have come across this type of fit index being reported by some folks to assess the fit of some CFA models they ran.  I was baffled by it and I question its validity as a goodness of fit measure for CFAs.  My understanding is that it's a type of R^2 for linear regression, or for the structural component of SEM, but not the measurement component of SEM, i.e., CFAs. My search through google scholar didn't give me any hits on papers describing CD being used for any type of CFAs. 

What do people think about this?  I'd appreciate any insights you may have. 

Thank you!

Anh

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: Coefficient of determination as a goodness of fit for CFAs
parts:
Decades ago, the LISREL package routinely reported coefficient of determination, and people tried to interpret it. It represents a collective R2 for all of the observed variables in the model (except covariates). You could also calculate one for the dependent factors in the model. As a multivariable R2, the idea was that higher values indicated stronger loadings, which generally meant higher power for the chi-square statistic. However, CD behaves in unexpected ways. A low R2 for a single variable could produce a low CD, even if all other R2 values are high. I don't know if LISEL even reports it anymore.

My cynical guess would be that some author decided to report it because the value was high, which, the author thought, made their model look good. For myself, I would not want to take CD even as a proxy for the individual R2 values--I would much rather see the individual R2s myself. As a "fit index"? Not worth anyone's time.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Coefficient of determination as a goodness of fit for CFAs
parts: Would you kindly explain why CD, when used as a fit index for CFAs, is not worth anyone's time?

It is not a fit index.  Your model could be perfectly specified even for data that have very low proportions of common-factor variance (and thus low CD).

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen
